name: clanker-skills
description: Reusable Claude Code tooling for understanding other repositories. Ships the Skills & Prompts Explorer: a build-explorer skill that discovers every skill, agent, and prompt in any repo and generates a self-contained, browsable static site with assessment cards and clickable, source-linked workflow diagrams.

plugins.name: adopt-repo
plugins.description: Onboard an upstream OSS repo into the dev workspace end to end: create a private <name>-dev mirror, give it an altien-main development trunk (main stays a pristine upstream mirror), vendor the explorer skills into the repo and push them so Claude in the cloud can build the documentation islands, pause for that cloud build, then pull the islands back and register them on the docs launcher. A sequencer over private-mirror, fork-trunk, the explorer skills, and rescan-docs. Exposes /adopt-repo.

plugins.name: skills-explorer
plugins.description: Discovers every skill, agent, prompt-template, system-prompt, and instruction doc in a repository and builds a self-contained, dependency-light static explorer: each artifact gets a structured assessment card, a programmatic-surface panel (tool grants, MCP servers, invocation mode, bundled resources), and a generated workflow diagram whose steps slice their verbatim source section.

plugins.name: private-mirror
plugins.description: Set up the current empty directory as a private mirror of a public GitHub repo — like a fork, but private: pull updates from upstream but never push to it. Disables GitHub Actions before the first push, rewires remotes so plain push/pull only touch your private copy, and physically disables pushing to upstream. Exposes /mirror-repo.

plugins.name: fork-trunk
plugins.description: Turn an existing GitHub fork into a clean two-branch setup: a fork-specific default development branch (e.g. <org>-main) that all your work lands on, while main stays a pristine mirror of upstream you only sync from. Creates the trunk off the upstream-synced main, sets it as the GitHub AND local default, routes unmerged local work onto it via PR (never onto main), and can disable GitHub Actions on the fork. Exposes /fork-trunk.

plugins.name: prd-reviewer
plugins.description: Builds a self-contained, static review harness for ONE PRD / design / epic — not the whole repo. Scopes a Markdown browser to a single PRD folder plus the source it references (driven by a referenced-files.txt list in the PRD folder), so a reviewer reads the design and clicks straight through to the real code. Sidebar leads with the PRD and groups referenced source (collapsed); source renders colour-coded, line-numbered, with brace folding; mermaid diagrams get a full-screen zoom/pan overlay. Quiet commenting: the panel stays closed until asked for, select text and right-click to comment, and commented passages get an inline marker you can click. Exposes /prd-reviewer.

plugins.name: repository-explorer
plugins.description: Builds a self-contained, static Repository Explorer for any repo: a browsable Markdown documentation site (file tree, search, rendered mermaid, and a review/commenting layer) plus a code-verified Architecture & Technology analysis published as both Markdown and expressive HTML with hand-authored inline-SVG diagrams. Browse the docs, then read an honest, source-linked walkthrough of how the system actually fits together. Exposes /repository-explorer.

plugins.name: atlas-explorer
plugins.description: Builds The Atlas for a repository: a live FastAPI documentation navigator that binds every markdown doc to the code it describes. Doc↔code 50/50 views (path mentions become chips; the panel shows tree-sitter-sliced, Pygments-highlighted source with fold regions and jump-to-symbol), SQLite FTS5 search, live drift detection (every doc→code reference verified against the tree, plus deterministic quantitative-claim counters), authored curation (per-doc summaries, sequenced journeys, clickable SVG flow diagrams), and anchored commenting with clipboard agent-brief export. The heavyweight, server-based sibling to the static explorers — self-contained and local, but with real Python dependencies. Exposes /build-atlas.
